text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lithuanian banking experts said that Estonian banks are too small to take over any bank in Lithuania.
- Russian oil concern Jukos said that it could boost its oil exports through Klaipeda by 2.5 times this year if Lithuania would reduce railway tariffs.
- Lithuania's economy ministry intends to choose Germany's Gesellschaft fur Nuclear-Behalter to supply nuclear waste vats for the Ignalina Nuclear Power plant, newspaper sources said.
- Kidney transplant operations will be started in Lithuania in the near future.
- Lithuanian finance minister Algirdas Shemeta said he expects to sell the troubled state-run Lithuanian State Commercial bank before the beginning of summer.

- Austria's Creditanstalt Investment bank said it has decided to participate in the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom. Merrill Lynch International and Nomura International are also considering the opportunity.
- Lithuania is ready to revise taxes on oil extraction if Danish investors would submitt a plan outlining their plans to increase investment in the sector.
- Russia's oil concern Jukos is likely to increase its exports via Klaipeda port and is seriously considering the possibility to invest in the country's oil sector.
- Hermis Bank decided to sell the new issue of 460,000 shares with face a value of 50 litas for 150 litas each.
